abstract: In the absence of world government, an effective treaty to control the emissions of greenhouse gases should be self-enforcing. A self-enforcing treaty has the property that, if a country expects other countries to abide by the treaty, it will be in the self-interest of that country to abide by the treaty too. (A difficulty with the Kyoto Protocol is that it does not appear to lay the groundwork for a self-enforcing treaty). A self-enforcing treaty can be modeled as a Nash equilibrium of a suitably defined dynamic game among a large number of sovereign countries of diverse sizes and economic capabilities. We study such a game and characterize its equilibria (typically there are many) and the global-Pareto-optimal solutions. We identify one of the equilibria, which we call “business as usual,” with the current situation. The multiplicity of equilibria provides an opportunity to move from the inefficient business-as-usual equilibrium to one or more equilibria that are Pareto-superior. Using a calibrated model with 184 countries, we give numerical illustrations of business-as-usual and global-Pareto-optimal trajectories and estimate the potential welfare gains from a self-enforcing treaty.
abstract_zh: 在没有世界政府的情况下，控制温室气体排放的有效条约应当是自我执行的。自我执行的条约具有如下性质：如果一国预期其他国家会遵守该条约，那么对该国而言，自身也遵守该条约符合其自身利益。（《京都议定书》的一个难点在于，它似乎并未为自我执行的条约奠定基础。）自我执行的条约可以被建模为由大量规模和经济能力各异的主权国家之间，一个经过适当定义的动态博弈的纳什均衡。我们研究了这样一个博弈，并刻画了其均衡（通常存在多个）以及全球帕累托最优解。我们将其中一个均衡，称为“一切照旧”，与当前的情况相对应。均衡的多重性为从低效的一切照旧均衡转向一个或多个帕累托改进的均衡提供了机会。我们利用一个包含184个国家的校准模型，对一切照旧轨迹和全球帕累托最优轨迹进行了数值说明，并估计了自我执行条约的潜在福利收益。
